messages:
alex: Quick sync — planning a coordinated inter-repo bump tomorrow 09:00 PT to runtime v0.15. This will include API (v1.8), console (v0.9.2), and JS/py SDK updates. Need confirmation on compatibility windows and any blockers.

maya: heads-up noted. I own console. main -> release/v0.15 cut at 08:00 PT? that gives CI an hour. :eyes:

leo: API: we have a minor schema bump (adds optional `session_metadata`) — should be backwards compatible but requires SDKs to accept unknown fields. compile-time check in clients may fail.

jess: SDKs: matt and I will land a tolerant parser in js-sdk and py-sdk. targeting a patch release for SDKs (js 2.4.1, py 1.7.1) that accepts `session_metadata`. we can cut at 08:30 PT.

matt: +1. will open the skeletal PRs now and link. plan: merge SDK compatibility first, then API, then runtime, then console. order reduces runtime->client break exposure.

alex: proposed order sounds good. timeline summary: 08:00 PT branch cut (release/v0.15), 08:30 SDKs merged & published to npm/pypi (pre-release tags), 09:00 runtime v0.15 deploy canary, 10:00 console rollout. does that work?

leo: one question: runtime v0.15 introduces a KV-cache key encoding change behind a feature flag. we will default OFF in canary. need API to expose feature-flag opt-in param for now.

jess: SDKs will expose `client.featureFlags.set('kvEncodingV2', true)` in the patch. will default false. add to changelog entry.

maya: console: will add a toggle in server config to enable kvEncodingV2 for envs that opt-in. no UI change needed for GA.

alex: sweet. can folks link PRs here when created and paste the changelog snippet we plan to publish? we should also remind docs to bump runtime example snippets. :memo:

matt: PRs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/js-sdk/pull/678, https://github.com/redwood-inference/py-sdk/pull/432 — both add tolerant parsing + featureFlags api.

leo: API PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/api/pull/214 adds `session_metadata` to /v1/generate request (optional) + tests.

alex: runtime PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1234 — KV encoding v2 behind flag, kernel changes, performance tests included. console PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/990 modifies server config and changelog.

matt: quick git snippet for the branch cut (for anyone doing manual cherry-picks):
```
git checkout -b release/v0.15 main
# cherry-pick critical commits
git cherry-pick <sha1> <sha2>
# open PR against release/v0.15
```

jess: changelog snippet (SDKs):
- js-sdk 2.4.1, py-sdk 1.7.1: add tolerant request parsing to accept optional `session_metadata` and add feature flag API `kvEncodingV2` (default: false).

maya: console changelog:
- console v0.9.2: add server-side toggle for KV encoding v2; no UI changes.

leo: API changelog:
- api v1.8: add optional `session_metadata` field to generation request. no breaking changes.

alex: anything blocking? security review? perf regressions?

matt: security: no new auth surface. perf: runtime perf tests show +2% CPU for certain kernels with kvEncodingV2 enabled; but default OFF. we should be safe.

jess: CI note: some flaky tests in js-sdk that fail on windows — I disabled the flaky case in a follow-up commit and marked it in the PR. will re-enable post-cutover.

alex: final checklist for tomorrow:
- [maya] cut release/v0.15 at 08:00 PT
- [matt,jess] merge SDK compatibility + publish pre-release by 08:30 PT
- [leo] merge API changes by 08:45 PT
- [alex] merge runtime PR and start canary at 09:00 PT (kvEncodingV2 OFF)
- [maya] start console rollout at 10:00 PT, switch knob for opt-ins after validation
- postmortem: track any client errors tagged `client:compat` and escalate to #incidents if >1% error rate

matt: pinging @release-bot to create a release checklist and remind on the hour. :rocket:

release-bot: Created release checklist https://go/release-checklists/2534561234 and scheduled reminders at 07:45, 08:20, 08:50, 09:50. CI status watcher set. :white_check_mark:

alex: perfect. i'll post a short note to #general with the user-facing maintenance window once the SDK pre-releases are public. thanks all :heart:
